correctness.rationale: Modulo 1 is vacuous; at a prime p the difference is (p+1)(p−2). For p², p³≡1 modulo D=p²+p+1, so the condition is D|p−3; the strict bound |p−3|<D gives p=3, and 9 satisfies the congruence. For 2q with q odd, reduction modulo q+1 gives a difference congruent to 2 and hence an impossibility. For two distinct odd primes there is even a direct check: 4 divides both nφ(n) and σ(n), since each p−1, q−1, p+1, q+1 is even. Thus nφ(n)−2 cannot be divisible by σ(n). The frozen proof's more detailed valuations are also correct. This exhausts Ω≤2 including the unit, without relying on the attached finite checker, which was inspected but not run. Mixed powers at higher Ω are outside the claim.

evidence: Dujella–Luca prove finiteness for each fixed finite support, give the {2,3} support classification and recall that 8 and 9 are the only composite prime powers. They say the details for extending the effective method to arbitrary fixed two-prime supports were not worked out. Bujačić gives the exact answers 1,2,5,8 for {2,5}.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A result stronger in the allowed multiplicities for two particular supports only excludes the semiprimes 6 and 10 there. Finiteness on each fixed support cannot imply the absence of variable pq. The stronger published prime-power classification does cover the p² slice and must be credited.
